summary: Dallas Morning News republishes a Bloomberg article on airline executives' reactions to Delta's AI pricing tests. The article says Delta frames its system as speeding analysis for long-standing dynamic pricing rather than targeting customers with personal data, while American's CEO rejects AI pricing as inappropriate. It includes Southwest CEO Bob Jordan's statement that Southwest has no plans to use AI in revenue management or pricing and is instead using AI mainly for customer service and customer inquiries.
key_excerpts: "Delta Air Lines plans to use AI to help set pricing on as much as 20% of its network by the end of this year." | "It is not using the technology to target customers using personal data, and all customers see the same fares in all retail channels, the carrier said in a statement." | "Southwest Airlines Co. also has no plans to use AI in revenue management or pricing, CEO Bob Jordan said." | "Pricing is very sophisticated," Jordan said. The system Southwest uses "is fairly mature and we're happy with it."

summary: CNBC reports on Southwest's first assigned-seat sales for flights beginning January 27, 2026, explaining that seat-selection prices vary by route, travel date, seat location, fare product, and demand. The article situates Southwest's change within a broader shift away from its historical open-seating model and toward ancillary revenue from seating, bags, and basic economy buy-ups. It includes a Southwest executive comment that assigned seating may make buying up from basic economy to Choice more compelling.

summary: Mundo Trip argues that Southwest's updated privacy policy gives the airline broad permission to collect and combine customer data, creating concern that the data could support personalized or surveillance pricing. The article emphasizes that Southwest has not confirmed using customer profiles to adjust fares or ancillary pricing, but says the policy language permits expanded tracking, profiling, retargeting, data sharing, automation, and AI training. It frames the privacy update as part of a broader industry move toward data-driven, segmented airline revenue practices.
